name: qip-core
purpose: The deterministic substrate every other crate is built on: fixed-point Decimal money, injected Clock/Rng (no ambient time or randomness), a typed Id per domain concept, a qip_core::error::Error with named constructors, and the `_FILE` secret-indirection helper every credential in the platform reads through.
key_contracts: IdGenerator + 18 typed ids (EventId, OrderId, PositionId, DecisionId, ...) (src/ids.rs)
Clock trait, SystemClock, ManualClock, Timestamp, Duration (src/time.rs)
production_evidence: Imported directly by every deployable binary's main.rs and by essentially every other crate in the workspace (62 Cargo.toml files depend on qip-core.workspace, confirmed by `grep -rl '^qip-core\.workspace' crates/*/*/Cargo.toml`); e.g. backend/crates/apps/qip-api/src/main.rs, qip-fastbrain/src/main.rs, qip-deepbrain/src/main.rs, qip-edge-node/src/main.rs and qip-cli/src/main.rs all construct a Clock/Context and read secrets through it.
io_and_state: No I/O of its own (a lib per the architecture boundary; enforced by the acceptance suite's architecture.rs). secret::from_environment reads process environment indirectly only insofar as the caller supplies the value via env(name) closures passed in by a composition root — the crate itself performs no std::env call. Clock/Rng are injected abstractions, not ambient I/O.
status_reason: Foundational and stable: zero TODO/stub markers found in src (grep for TODO|FIXME|unimplemented!|todo!|stub found none), 89 tests including FIPS/RFC vectors, used pervasively across all 62 workspace crates that declare it.
gaps_observed: None found: no TODO/FIXME/unimplemented!/todo!/stub markers in backend/crates/libs/qip-core/src (verified by grep across all 13 files).

name: qip-contracts
purpose: The shared vocabulary between edge cells and the central plane — bitemporal Stamped facts, attributed Origin, the nine-deduction NetEdge cost decomposition, capital envelopes/grants, promotion gates, governance approvals, and the wire message/policy payload shapes both sides serialize.
key_contracts: AllocationMode, Capability, DegradationState, Freshness, StrategyClass (src/degradation.rs, 921 lines, largest module)
Approval, Control, Entitlement, Provenance, Severity, Usage (src/governance.rs)
production_evidence: 31 workspace Cargo.toml files depend on it including every apps/* binary except qip-web; direct non-test use confirmed in backend/crates/apps/qip-api/src/{web.rs,statement.rs,routes.rs,mesh.rs}, qip-deepbrain/src/{evolution.rs,discovery.rs,succession.rs,main.rs}, qip-edge-node/src/{feed.rs,arbitrage.rs,venue.rs,main.rs,cross_region.rs,reprice.rs,strategies.rs,gateway.rs}.
io_and_state: No I/O (a lib). Pure types and validation logic — e.g. NetEdge refuses construction if its parts do not sum (per module doc), Stamped enforces valid-time <= known-time.
status_reason: No stub/TODO markers in src; the only 'simulat*' hits are legitimate domain vocabulary (GateStage::Simulated, wire.rs's `simulated: bool` field on an order envelope). Depended on by 31 crates including the edge hot path and the central plane.
gaps_observed: None structural. gate.rs:15-19 documents GateStage::Researched/Simulated as legitimate lifecycle stages, not incomplete code.

name: qip-events
purpose: The typed, hash-chained event backbone: every payload declares a Topic and schema version through EventBody so publishing to the wrong topic fails to compile; EventBus dispatches breadth-first for deterministic replay; EventLog chains each record to its predecessor's hash so a truncated or edited audit trail is detectable.
key_contracts: Topic, TopicGroup (src/topic.rs, 667 lines, every event topic name)
production_evidence: 22 workspace crates depend on it; non-test use confirmed in backend/crates/apps/qip-api/src/{web.rs,mesh.rs,console.rs,stream.rs,routes.rs}, qip-cli/src/{replay.rs,demo/mod.rs}, qip-deepbrain/src/{discovery.rs,node.rs,campaign.rs,main.rs,evolution.rs} — e.g. EventLog is opened at start-up alongside ChainArchive in every central-plane binary.
io_and_state: EventLog persists via the injected KeyValueStore/file backend from qip-storage or qip-core::kv; append() computes SHA-256 over sequence+previous_hash+canonical event (src/log.rs:135,679-712). No direct filesystem or network calls inside qip-events itself — durability is delegated to whatever store the caller wires in.
status_reason: Hash-chained EventLog with crash-recovery tests (truncation, torn writes) in the sibling qip-storage engine test suite; wired into every central binary's composition root.
gaps_observed: None found: only 'simulat*' hits are the Topic::Simulate/SimulationStarted/SimulationCompleted enum variants (src/topic.rs:44,360-361), legitimate domain vocabulary, not stubs.

name: qip-storage
purpose: Persistence ports (KeyValueStore, BlobStore) and their adapters: in-memory and file-per-document for tests/dev, an embedded write-ahead-log DurableStore engine for the one target this platform actually runs durably, a Redis/Memorystore RESP client as a cache only, and GCP Cloud Storage / BigQuery JSON REST adapters that speak through qip-transport's plaintext HTTP client behind a required TLS-terminating proxy.
key_contracts: Durability, DurableStore, EngineConfig, EngineStats, WriteBatch (src/engine/mod.rs, 906 lines, WAL + checkpoints + crash recovery)
gcp::{CloudStorageBlobStore, BigQueryWarehouse, GcpAccess, AccessToken, TokenSource, MetadataServerTokens} (src/gcp/*, 2397 lines)
production_evidence: StorageSettings + ChainArchive are wired at start-up in every central binary's main.rs (qip-api, qip-fastbrain, qip-deepbrain, qip-cli, qip-edge-node, all `use qip_storage::ChainArchive` + `qip_storage::settings::StorageSettings`), and StorageSettings::key_value() dispatches to Memory/File/Engine adapters, which ARE reached in production. BUT: Terraform's storage_target variable validates only {memory,file,engine} (infrastructure/terraform/variables.tf:376-382 `contains(["memory","file","engine"], var.storage_target)`), so the gcp/{storage,bigquery} and redis adapters, though fully implemented and unit-tested, are structurally unreachable from any deployed environment's configuration surface — confirmed no `grep -rl 'CloudStorageBlobStore\|BigQueryWarehouse\|RedisKeyValueStore\|StorageProvider' backend/crates/apps/*/src` hits outside tests.
io_and_state: fsio.rs flushes every write to the storage device before reporting success (src/fsio.rs). File/Engine adapters write to a local root path; Cloud Run workloads (qip-api/fastbrain/deepbrain) run with QIP_STORAGE_TARGET=memory in every gitops environment (infrastructure/gitops/envs/{dev,stage,prod}/*.yaml — confirmed dev/api.yaml:72-73 `QIP_STORAGE_TARGET: memory`), so central-plane state does not survive a Cloud Run restart today. Only infrastructure/terraform/modules/execution-node's startup script sets QIP_STORAGE_TARGET=engine, QIP_STORAGE_ROOT=/var/lib/qip/journal (infrastructure/terraform/modules/execution-node/templates/startup.sh.tftpl:184-185), but no environment currently provisions an execution_node (execution_nodes = {} everywhere per the observability domain doc). gcp adapters reach the network only through qip_transport::HttpClient (plaintext HTTP/1.1, requires an external TLS-terminating proxy the adapter itself never assumes).
status_reason: The three implemented-and-deployable targets (memory/file/engine) are hardened and reached from production; the six managed-target ports (gcp Cloud Storage/BigQuery implemented but Terraform-unreachable; AlloyDb/Spanner/Bigtable not even implemented, refusing construction by design) are code-complete or intentionally absent but never selected by any environment.
gaps_observed: AlloyDb/Spanner/Bigtable are not implemented at all — StorageTarget::is_implemented() excludes them (src/provider.rs:62-72), required_configuration() names the missing PostgreSQL/gRPC client for each (src/provider.rs:192-260).

gcp::{CloudStorageBlobStore,BigQueryWarehouse} and redis::RedisKeyValueStore are fully implemented and unit-tested but never selectable in any deployed environment because Terraform's storage_target variable validation admits only memory|file|engine (infrastructure/terraform/variables.tf:376-382).

Every Cloud Run environment (dev/stage/prod) sets QIP_STORAGE_TARGET=memory, so the only durable target (engine) is reached solely by the execution-node startup script, and no environment currently provisions an execution node (infrastructure/environments/*/terraform.tfvars execution_nodes = {}).

name: qip-transport
purpose: The in-tree streaming backbone that replaced Google Pub/Sub per ADR 0011: an HTTP/1.1 client on std::net::TcpStream with the same bounded-body/timeout discipline as the API server, and a mesh transport carrying qip_events::AnyEvent frames with bounded retry, backpressure, dead-lettering and at-least-once (never exactly-once) delivery — explicitly plaintext and unauthenticated, relying on VPC-level network isolation rather than any in-tree TLS or handshake.
key_contracts: ClientLimits, HttpClient, HttpError, HttpRequest, HttpResponse, Method, Url (src/http.rs, 1465 lines)
Admission, Delivery, MeshConfig, MeshEndpoint, MeshInbox, MeshMessage, MeshPublisher, PollRequest/Response, RemoteSubscriber (src/mesh.rs, 1243 lines)
OutboundQueue, QueueStats (src/queue.rs — refuses with QueueFull, never drops)
production_evidence: 17 workspace crates depend on it. Directly wired at start-up: backend/crates/apps/qip-api/src/main.rs:318-320 calls `qip_api::mesh::MeshBackbone::open(...)` from `MeshSettings::from_env()`; backend/crates/apps/qip-edge-node/src/mesh.rs constructs MeshLink over qip_transport::breaker::{BreakerState,BreakerPolicy} and ClientLimits/MeshConfig/RetryPolicy (lines 55-280). Also used by qip-brokers, qip-market-ingestion, qip-streaming, qip-training, qip-chain, qip-reasoning-engine, qip-data-finder services.
io_and_state: http.rs opens raw std::net::TcpStream connections with explicit connect/read/write timeouts, one connection per request, one thread per publisher — no async runtime. No TLS: module doc (lib.rs:45-75) states production must add mutual TLS via a service-mesh sidecar, which is not implemented in this crate and not deployed. spool.rs persists an outbound backlog through an injected qip_core::KeyValueStore for durability across restarts.
status_reason: Fully implemented and reached from production wiring at qip-api and qip-edge-node, with dedicated reliability/mesh/breaker/http_client test suites; the module's own documentation names the missing production requirement (mutual TLS) as an open item rather than a hidden gap.
gaps_observed: No TLS and no peer authentication by design; module doc states 'Production must add mutual TLS' via a service mesh sidecar, not yet present in any deployed manifest (backend/crates/libs/qip-transport/src/lib.rs:45-63).

Delivery is at-least-once only; every consumer of the transport must independently be idempotent (backend/crates/libs/qip-transport/src/lib.rs:30-43) — this is a documented architectural constraint, not a defect, but is a requirement any blueprint-driven consumer must satisfy.

name: qip-observability
purpose: Traces, metrics, structured logs and SLOs with OpenTelemetry-compatible semantics (trace/span ids, span kinds, histogram buckets) implemented in-tree so the platform can report on itself even when no external collector is reachable; bundled as one Telemetry{metrics,tracer,logger} handed to every component.
production_evidence: 10 workspace crates depend on it; Telemetry is constructed and served in every central binary — backend/crates/apps/qip-api/src/routes.rs:79,1249 exposes `/metrics` via Prometheus text exposition (`scrape(&platform)`), and `Platform::` in qip-kernel records to it at 55 call sites (`grep -c 'metrics\.\(count\|gauge\|increment\|observe[a-z_]*\)\(' backend/crates/runtime/qip-kernel/src/platform.rs` = 55).
io_and_state: No network I/O of its own — metrics/traces/logs are held in-process (Metrics holds counters/gauges/histograms behind internal state; Histogram buckets observations). Exposition (Prometheus text, OTLP-shaped JSON) is rendered on demand by the calling app's HTTP handler, not pushed anywhere by this crate.
status_reason: The library itself is complete, tested and reached from production recording sites and a live /metrics route; the platform-level gap is downstream of this crate — nothing has been proven to scrape any deployed process (infrastructure/terraform/variables.tf:1136-1158 workload_metrics_exist default = false), so recorded metrics exist but are not yet ingested by Cloud Monitoring anywhere.
gaps_observed: Emission and the /metrics route are proven, but ingestion is not: workload_metrics_exist defaults to false and every Cloud Monitoring alert policy in infrastructure/terraform/modules/observability is gated on it (infrastructure/terraform/variables.tf:1136-1158). This is an infrastructure-layer gap, not a defect in qip-observability itself.

name: qip-confidential
purpose: Statistical disclosure control for cross-cell aggregates — a cohort threshold, a per-cell monotone privacy budget, Laplace noise seeded from qip_core::Xoshiro256, and a pairwise differencing gate — so a console/research consumer can see an aggregate (mean gross notional, total realised loss) across regional cells without any single cell's book being recoverable. Explicitly NOT confidential computing: no enclave, no attestation, no encryption, no cryptographic protocol; the aggregator sees every raw contribution in memory, and the defence is entirely on the arithmetic of what leaves the gate.
key_contracts: NoiseScale, Sensitivity, noise_for(), snap() (src/noise.rs — Laplace mechanism)
NOT_DEFENDED_AGAINST: [&str; 8] (src/lib.rs:181-191, the threat table as data)
production_evidence: Depended on by exactly one workspace crate, qip-kernel (grep -rl '^qip-confidential\.workspace' backend/crates/*/*/Cargo.toml → 1 file: backend/crates/runtime/qip-kernel/Cargo.toml). qip-kernel's central/insights.rs wraps it as CellInsights, and Platform::new unconditionally constructs a CellInsights (backend/crates/runtime/qip-kernel/src/platform.rs:358,4441), so the gate IS built in every deployed process's composition path. But its two public query methods (CellInsights::mean_gross_notional, ::total_realised_loss) and the accessor Platform::insights_mut are never called anywhere outside backend/crates/runtime/qip-kernel/tests/insights.rs — confirmed by `grep -rn 'insights_mut\|mean_gross_notional\|total_realised_loss' backend/crates/apps backend/crates/runtime --include='*.rs'` matching only the definition sites and the test file; no apps/*/src route (console, API, CLI) references 'insight' at all.
io_and_state: No I/O — pure in-process arithmetic over Decimal-derived f64 contributions. PrivacyLedger and ReleaseGate hold their state (spent epsilon per cell, release history) only in memory for the lifetime of the owning Platform; nothing here persists a ledger to disk, so budget spend does not survive a process restart.
status_reason: The crate itself is fully implemented, extensively tested (53 tests including an explicit differencing-attack demonstration) and wired into Platform's constructor, but its module doc says plainly it was 'reachable from nothing' before qip-kernel's insights.rs wrapper, and that wrapper's own query methods still have zero production callers today — the gate is built every cycle but never asked a question outside tests.
gaps_observed: CellInsights::mean_gross_notional and ::total_realised_loss (backend/crates/runtime/qip-kernel/src/central/insights.rs:75-109) are constructed via Platform::insights_mut (backend/crates/runtime/qip-kernel/src/platform.rs:5377) but that accessor has no caller in backend/crates/apps/**/src outside tests — no console route, API endpoint or CLI command surfaces a cross-cell insight.

PrivacyLedger's spend state is process-memory only; a restart resets every cell's spent epsilon with no persistence layer, which the crate's own doc does not claim to address (no [`qip_core::KeyValueStore`] usage anywhere in backend/crates/libs/qip-confidential/src).
evidence: grep -rn 'insights_mut|mean_gross_notional|total_realised_loss' backend/crates/apps backend/crates/runtime → matches only definitions + backend/crates/runtime/qip-kernel/tests/insights.rs
